title: Canary-aware synthetic workload probes for upgrade-safe VPC rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a canary-aware synthetic traffic probe suite for VPC/private deployments that produces multi-dimensional SLO signals (p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate buckets, token-throughput, request-saturation) and ties them to canary cohorts during platform upgrades. The goal is to detect regressions introduced during rolling upgrades or quantized model swaps before they affect customer traffic, while avoiding noisy false positives from transient load changes.

Rationale: Current VPC health probes capture basic liveness and some token throughput metrics, but we lack a reproducible synthetic workload that mirrors customer token distributions and can be selectively routed to canary cohorts. Upgrades to runtime kernels, KV cache changes, or autoscaler tuning can impact tail latency and token-flow saturation in subtle ways; we need probes that: (1) exercise KV cache hit/miss profiles, (2) generate variable sequence-length traffic, and (3) measure per-request token emission rates so SLO alerts are meaningful during canaries.

Design overview:
- Synthetic driver: a small, containerized probe that can be deployed as a sidecar or as a dedicated probe job inside customer VPCs (configurable via Terraform module). The driver supports workload templates (short prompts, long-context prompts, high-throughput micro-requests) and a token-generator harness to simulate streaming.
- Canary scoping: Probes will be attachable to canary subsets using deployment tags. During an upgrade rollout, the orchestration will spin up a probe cohort targeting only the canary instances and another baseline cohort targeting a stable set.
- Signals collected: p50/p95/p99 generation latency, request error rate (4xx/5xx split), token throughput per-second, queue/backpressure indicators (request queue length, enqueue delay), KV cache hit ratio, and model-variant fallback counts.
- Baseline & dynamic thresholds: For each signal we will compute a short-term baseline (rolling 1h median) and long-term baseline (7d median) and trigger alerts when canary diverges > X sigma from baseline or when absolute SLO thresholds (eg p95 > 250ms, error-rate > 0.5%) are exceeded. Thresholds will be configurable per-customer-class.

Acceptance criteria: See acceptance_criteria field below.

Implementation phases:
1) Prototype probe binary + local harness that can be run against a dev VPC (2 wks).
2) Terraform module to deploy probe jobs and connect Metering/Prometheus exporters (1 wk).
3) Canary orchestration integration: tie probes into rollout controller so probes are created/destroyed as canary cohorts change (1 wk).
4) Alerting and dashboards: Grafana dashboard + PagerDuty rules and automated rollback hook via rollout controller (1 wk).
5) Runbook and docs: playbooks for interpreting signals and SRE runbook for emergency rollback (3 days).

Rollout plan: Start with non-production test accounts, validate sensitivity and false-positive rate over 1 week, iterate thresholds, then enable for small set of customers on Dedicated/Dusty tiers, then expand to all Private deployments.

Links: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Canary+Synthetic+Probes (placeholder), GH prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/probe-suite/pull/42 (placeholder), Slack thread: #infra-probes-upgrades
acceptance_criteria: Probe binary can be launched inside a customer VPC test environment and produce the full set of signals to Prometheus/StatsD
Terraform module exists and supports canary scoping via labels/tags and RBAC constraints
Rollout controller creates canary probe cohorts automatically during canary deployments and tears them down on completion
Grafana dashboard visualizing baseline vs canary for p50/p95/p99, error-rate, token throughput, KV hit ratio
Alert rule prototype triggers at configurable divergence thresholds and invokes rollback webhook when configured
SRE runbook documented with clear triage steps and sample queries for investigating probe regressions
runbook: Triage step 1: Confirm probe health in the canary cohort (probe job pod status, exporter metrics present). Step 2: Compare canary short-term baseline vs 7d baseline on the dashboard. Step 3: If canary error-rate or p95 breach exceeds configured threshold, identify correlated signals: token_throughput_per_sec and kv_cache_hit_ratio. Step 4: If KV hit ratio drops with increased p95, rollback runtime change or enable cache warmup. Step 5: If saturation observed (queue length growth) engage autoscaler override or reduce canary traffic via rollout controller. Step 6: Escalate to on-call runtime engineer and file postmortem if customer-facing impact observed.
notes: We must avoid creating probes that look like DDoS — rate limits and egress policies must be enforced per-VPC.
Prototype should include a deterministic workload template generator so we can run A/B comparisons across code versions.
Consider shipping an opt-in shim in the Terraform module so customers can enable probes during maintenance windows only.
